name: San Antone
summary: Carson NF lookout on San Antonio Mountain: planned by 1911, lightning-struck cabin in 1918; listed gone, no removal date found.
design: Lookout cabin with a short tower attached (NRHP nomination). A 1918 newspaper item describes a one-floor house about 12 by 12 feet with walls almost wholly of glass. The accounts do not match.
status_note: Listed as gone on the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. No source dates its removal or describes the lookout site now; the summit has radio and television towers.
agency: USDA Forest Service, Carson National Forest

access.note: On Carson National Forest land on San Antonio Mountain. Wikipedia says Forest Road 418 has a locked gate where it crosses private property and may not be open to motorized travel by the general public.

events.note: A line was to be built to San Antone Mountain, where a lookout station for forest fires would be established. The item is a plan; it does not say when the station was finished.
Lightning struck the cabin on the night of June 18, 1918 and tore a hole two feet square in the roof. The lookoutman was not hurt.
Lookoutman Mr. Ground was in the lookout house on the night of June 18, 1918.
